title: Finite-stage local module descent data
statement: Let $I$ be a directed preorder, $R:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a functor with Noetherian rings $R_k$, and $c$ a limit cone of $R^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\operatorname{Spec}$ with affine vertex $S$. Fix $i\in I$ and a quasi-compact, quasi-separated, locally finitely presented morphism $f:X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$ [def-pc-scheme]. Put $X=X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)} S$, and $X_j=X_i\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)}\operatorname{Spec}(R_j)$ for $j\geq i$ [def-pc-base-change]. For a finitely presented quasi-coherent module $M$ on $X$ [pqf-def-coherent], there are $j\geq i$, a finite affine open cover $u_a:U_a\to X_j$, and a module descent datum $D$ on that cover (modules $D_a$, compatible invertible overlap maps satisfying the cocycle), with each $D_a$ finitely presented and quasi-coherent, such that pulling back $D$ along $p:X\to X_j$ yields a descent datum isomorphic to the restriction datum of $M$ on the pulled-back cover. No global module on $X_j$ is asserted.

source.place: Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-modules-finite-presentation, Tag 01ZR, first proof: finite affine covers and overlap compatibility

proof.text: Apply local object lifting to obtain a finite affine cover U at stage j with local finitely presented quasi-coherent models N and componentwise pullback comparisons to M. Choose the comparisons within the proof, and apply eventual overlap compatibility for these supplied models. Obtain k >= j, the pulled-back cover V, descent data D with components isomorphic to the pulled-back N, and a compatible comparison morphism eta with invertible components.

The base-change map Xk -> Xj is affine because it is the base change of Spec(Rk) -> Spec(Rj). Thus the finite pullback cover V is affine. Pullback preserves finite presentation and quasi-coherence, and invariance under the supplied component isomorphisms gives those properties for D. Build an isomorphism of descent data from asIso(eta.hom a) using DescentData.isoMk and eta.comm. The index i <= k is the transitive composite of i <= j and j <= k.
